# The remediation round of stage 1 runs the whole example in the real engine: a round on the branch integration/s1 of a trunk integration/r1,
# a trunk move that the sync lands, one child item through plan, implement, the draft, the gate, the review and the landing, and then the owner's wait.
# The tracker is the local one, the forge is the stand-in of the swarm scripts over a bare repository, and the agents and the remedy tool are fake programs of the PATH.
#
# The project file holds three settings that stand in for a machine of stage 1: source_checkout names a checkout (the agent steps forbid writes to it, and refuse when none is named),
# the owner is the login of the agent (the stand-in forge authors every pull request as "agent", so the owner must be that login), and the host block is a stand-in (see e2e_round_test.go).
# The host gate path is not covered by this script: the stand-in host builds locally and the gate check record is injected, so the host checks of the gate
# (among them the check that the folder of the round is clean) never run here.
isolate

exec git init -q -b main seed
exec git -C seed add Makefile .gitignore
exec git -C seed -c user.name=seed -c user.email=seed@example.com commit -q -m start
exec git clone -q --bare seed remote.git
exec git --git-dir=remote.git branch integration/r1 main
exec git --git-dir=remote.git branch integration/s1 main

# The trunk moved by one commit. The sync branch is the round branch with the trunk merged into it.
exec git clone -q remote.git syncclone
exec git -C syncclone checkout -q -b integration/r1 origin/integration/r1
cp moved.txt syncclone/moved.txt
exec git -C syncclone add moved.txt
exec git -C syncclone -c user.name=seed -c user.email=seed@example.com commit -q -m 'trunk moved'
exec git -C syncclone push -q origin integration/r1
exec git -C syncclone checkout -q -b sync/s1 origin/integration/s1
exec git -C syncclone -c user.name=seed -c user.email=seed@example.com merge -q --no-ff -m 'merge the trunk' integration/r1
exec git -C syncclone push -q origin sync/s1

example remediation/workflow.star flow/workflow.star

# The login folder of the runners is a credential path, so it holds nothing else: the state folder of beehave lies outside it, and an agent may read the data file.
mkdir forge
mkdir home
mkdir login
# The config folder of the runner holds the review skill that the prompts declare, as an installed user skill.
mkdir login/skills/the-review-skill
cp skill.md login/skills/the-review-skill/SKILL.md
env SWARM_REMOTE=$WORK/remote.git
env SWARM_FORGE=$WORK/forge
env HOME=$WORK/home

# The user of a project has a global git identity. The sandbox of an agent step refuses to start without one, and the worktree has no config of its own.
exec git config --file home/.gitconfig user.name e2e
exec git config --file home/.gitconfig user.email e2e@example.com
cp base forge/base
cp base forge/open-on-create

# The setup of the scripts writes a runner file whose login folder is the work folder. That folder holds the state folder, so the script puts its own runners in place.
cp runners.star config/runners.star
subst fake/claude fake/remedy config/projects/round.star config/runners.star
chmod 755 fake/claude
chmod 755 fake/remedy

exec beehaveround item add round round/integration/s1 --title 'The round' --body-file round.txt
exec beehaveround item add round 432 --title 'The child' --body-file child.txt

exec beehaveround run round/integration/s1 round --workflow flow/workflow.star &
waitstatus 'paused: The round has no item it can move'
exec beehaveround status
stdout 'item-432-r1	done'
stdout 'item 432 is not in the queue: it is closed'
exec beehaveround answer round/integration/s1 --as agent STOP
wait
stdout 'finished'

# The sync landed, the child ran each step once, and the landing merged its pull request into the round branch. The forge opened three pull requests: the sync into the round branch,
# the integration of the round into the trunk, and the child on the round branch.
grep -count=1 '^sync_review$' calls.log
grep -count=1 '^plan$' calls.log
grep -count=1 '^implement$' calls.log
grep -count=2 '^review$' calls.log
grep -count=2 '^MergePR ' forge/calls.log
grep -count=1 '^integration/s1$' forge/opened-1
grep -count=1 '^integration/r1$' forge/opened-2
grep -count=1 '^integration/s1$' forge/opened-3
# The child branch starts at the tip of the round branch after the sync land, not at the trunk branch: its parent holds the commit that the trunk moved.
exec git --git-dir=remote.git show 432^:moved.txt
stdout '^moved$'
exec git --git-dir=remote.git show integration/s1:432.txt
stdout '^432$'
exec git --git-dir=remote.git show integration/s1:moved.txt
stdout '^moved$'

-- base --
integration/s1
-- round.txt --
The round of the stage.
-- child.txt --
Change one thing.
-- seed/Makefile --
check: ; @mkdir -p reports && echo '<testsuite tests="1"><testcase name="t"/></testsuite>' > reports/r.xml
-- seed/.gitignore --
reports/
-- moved.txt --
moved
-- mutation.sh --
exit 0
-- skill.md --
---
name: the-review-skill
---
-- runners.star --
agents(max_concurrent = 2)
runner(name = "one", agent = "claude", config_dir = "@WORK@/login")
runner(name = "two", agent = "claude", config_dir = "@WORK@/login")
-- config/projects/round.star --
project(
    repo = "o/r",
    source = "file://@WORK@/remote.git",
    forge = "github",
    base_branch = "integration/r1",
    gate = "make check",
    test_report = "reports/*.xml",
    build_host = "build",
    host = host(provider = "ssh", disk_floor_gb = 50, slots = {"mutation": 1}, ssh = ssh(address = "10.0.0.5")),
    vars = {
        "round": {"base": "integration/s1", "owner": "agent", "owner_email": "agent@example.com", "lane_cap": 1, "fix_rounds": 2, "items": ["432"], "merge": True, "wait_hours": 72, "source_checkout": "/own/checkout"},
        "mutation_command": ["sh", "mutation.sh"],
        "review_skill": "the-review-skill",
    },
)
-- flow/prompts/plan.md --

write={{ .output_file }}
-- flow/prompts/implement.md --

-- flow/prompts/sync.md --

-- flow/prompts/sync_review.md --
step=sync_review
write={{ .output_file }}
-- flow/prompts/take_review.md --
step=take_review
-- fake/claude --
#!/bin/sh
if [ "$1" = --version ]; then echo "2.1.290 (Claude Code)"; exit 0; fi
prompt=$(cat)
field() { printf '%s\n' "$prompt" | sed -n "s/^$1=//p"; }
step=$(field step)
echo "$step" >> @WORK@/calls.log
echo '{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_skill","name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"the-review-skill"}}]}}'
echo '{"type":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_skill","content":"Launching skill: the-review-skill"}]}}'
case $step in
  plan) printf '{"regressions":"0"}\n' > "$(field write)" ;;
  review) printf '{"verdict":"approve","mechanism":"","regressions":"0","open":"","findings":"[]"}\n' > "$(field write)" ;;
  sync_review) printf '{"verdict":"approve"}\n' > "$(field write)" ;;
  sweep) printf '{"report":"# Report\\n"}\n' > "$(field write)" ;;
  implement)
    id=$(basename "$(pwd)")
    echo "$id" > "$id.txt"
    git add "$id.txt"
    git -c user.name=dev -c user.email=agent@example.com commit -q -m "task $id"
    git push -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$id"
    printf '{"report":"# Report\\n","uncaused":"[]"}\n' > "$(field write)"
    ;;
esac
echo '{"type":"result","subtype":"success","session_id":"s1","result":"done"}'
-- fake/remedy --
#!/bin/sh
# The remedy tool of the round runs only the read-only report step, which passes. The gate list is `beehave check gate-list`, which these rounds do not call. The forge writes run in the engine, on the forge of the script.
exit 0
